Offline MyInvois validation. A document can now be checked against the rules
LHDN enforces before it is submitted, instead of learning them one rejection at
a time.

Two of those rules were learned exactly that way: `CV317` and the consolidated
classification code came from having LHDN's preprod API reject a real
submission, and the shapes pinned as passing are the ones it then accepted.

## Validating

```ts
const { valid, issues } = myInvois.validate(invoice);
```

The result is shaped like LHDN's own response — a verdict alongside the detail
— so the offline check and the API's answer can be handled by one code path.
`myInvois.finalize(invoice)` runs the same rules and throws
`MyInvoisValidationError` instead, carrying every issue on `.issues`.

Every issue is reported at once, never just the first. That is a direct lesson
from the live API: LHDN returned an `ERR205` against the buyer's
`PartyIdentification` for a document whose faults were in the postal address
and the item classification code. The element its `propertyPath` named was
never wrong, and fixing one reported error at a time did not converge.

## What is checked

| Code | |
| --- | --- |
| `MYI004` | a required element is absent, or present but empty |
| `MYI001` | a required attribute was dropped |
| `MYI002` | a party has no TIN |
| `CV317`, `MYI003` | a consolidated e-Invoice is internally inconsistent |

`MYI001` exists because scalar params accept a bare `string` as shorthand for
the `Udt*` classes, and a bare string carries no attributes — so
`taxAmount: '0.00'` emits an amount with no `currencyID`, which is schema-valid
and rejected on submission.

`MYI004` also catches this library's one silent failure: a plain object passed
where a component instance is required emits an empty element rather than
raising, so `partyLegalEntities: [{ registrationName: 'X' }]` yields
`<cac:PartyLegalEntity/>` and loses the name without a word.

## What is deliberately not checked

A rule is admitted only if it is decidable from the document alone and cannot
reject a document LHDN accepts — a validator that blocks valid invoices is
worse than none, because the only workaround is to stop using it. Presence
rules are admitted only when the element appears in **both** documents this
repo knows LHDN accepted.

So `cbc:PostalZone`, `cbc:TaxCurrencyCode`, `cbc:InvoicedQuantity` and its
`unitCode` are all excluded: LHDN models each as an optional field in its own
right. Anything needing LHDN's own state — whether a TIN exists, whether it
matches your credentials — is left to the API, and monetary totals stay out
because MyInvois deviates from EN 16931 on `cbc:AllowanceTotalAmount`.

Only the fields common to every Invoice type are checked. Credit, debit and
refund notes also require `cac:BillingReference`, and the self-billed types
swap which party carries what; neither is checked, because neither has been
submitted.

## Breaking

`myInvois.finalize` was a no-op at document version 1.0 and now validates,
throwing on an invalid document. `myInvois.withSigner(...).finalize` validates
before signing. To build without the check, do not call `finalize`; to sign
without it, call `signInvoice` directly.

`validateInvoice` returns `{ valid, issues }` rather than a bare array.

See MIGRATION.md.

## Also

Dependencies refreshed, clearing twelve advisories including one critical —
all of them dev-only; the published package's single runtime dependency was
already clean. `xpath` removed, as nothing imported it.
